annotation.cut_point:
We are given the polynomial identity:

$$
(x^3 - 1)(x + 1)^7 = a_0 + a_1(x+3) + a_2(x+3)^2 + \cdots + a_{10}(x+3)^{10}
$$

We are to find the value of:

$$
a_0 + a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10}
$$

---

### Step 1: Understand the problem

We're given a polynomial expressed in terms of powers of $ (x+3) $, and we are to find the **sum of the coefficients** of this expansion. 

That is, evaluate the **sum of all coefficients** of the polynomial on the **right-hand side**.

But the right-hand side is a **polynomial in terms of $ (x+3) $**. So, to find the sum of all coefficients of that polynomial, we can evaluate the polynomial at $ x = -3 $, because:

$$
\text{Sum of coefficients} = P(-3)
$$

where $ P(x) $ is the polynomial on the right-hand side.
